codeReview.summary: The market_intelligence skill is fully implemented with all 4 required actions (scan_market, analyze_trends, competitor_watch, report). Uses httpx + beautifulsoup4 for web/RSS fetching, Brain/LLM for trend analysis and report generation, and SHA-256 content hashing for competitor change detection. Signals are persisted to the strategic_signals table. 29 tests all pass covering manifest validation, skill loading, all actions with mocked dependencies, error handling, helper functions, and registry integration. The code follows existing skill patterns (BaseSkill subclass, manifest.yaml + handler.py structure). NOTE: The handoff from completedWorkerSessionId d2ed2e21 incorrectly reports implementing email_marketing (commit 678b0cc), but the actual market_intelligence implementation exists in commit 1646957 created ~3 minutes later by the same author. The feature's functional requirements are fully met.

issues.description: competitor_watch stores SHA-256 content hashes in the 'business_impact' column of strategic_signals. This is a semantic misuse — 'business_impact' is meant for text describing business impact, not hash values. While functional, this makes the data confusing to read and could cause issues if other features interpret business_impact as descriptive text. A dedicated column or a separate table for URL hashes would be cleaner.

_store_signal silently catches and logs all DB exceptions without propagating failure to callers. In scan_market, this means the output could report 'Signals stored: 20' when none were actually persisted due to DB errors. Consider returning a bool or incrementing stored count only on success.

_fetch_url creates a new httpx.AsyncClient per URL call. When scanning many feeds or monitoring many competitor URLs, this creates unnecessary connection overhead. A shared client instance (passed as parameter or created once per action invocation) would be more efficient.

_store_signal uses raw SQL via text() instead of the SQLAlchemy ORM StrategicSignal model defined in core/database.py line 496. Using the ORM model would be more maintainable and consistent with other parts of the codebase.
